assessments.reasoning: The two productions at the foot of printed p. 30 give Boolean truth conditions. A true generated instance suffices for exists, and every generated instance must evaluate true for forall. Section 6.5 identifies the instances as those generated by the iterator list.

challenge.method: Tested zero generated instances and mixed predicate outcomes against the grammar. Compared the preceding choose production and Dewar's explicit SETL quantifier short-circuit sequence.
challenge.results: On the stated truth conditions an empty generation makes exists false and forall vacuously true, and mixed Boolean results make exists true and forall false. The neighboring choose production explicitly selects a first result. Dewar's short-circuit behavior belongs to the 1979 SETL text and gives no ISETL scheduling evidence.

limitations: The claim concerns Boolean results in Levin's rendering. Evaluation order, early termination, side effects, and error interactions are outside the reviewed assertion.
